topic: Static, dynamic and total pressure, principle of A.S.I, Indicated, rectified, equivalent and true air speed, errors in A.S.I.
syllabus_extract: Static, dynamic and total pressure, principle of A.S.I, Indicated, rectified, equivalent and true air speed, errors in A.S.I.
specific_objectives: 6.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the properties of atmosphere, flow over bodies, boundary layer.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Activity: Demonstration of pressure types using Pitot-static model. Safety: Handle glass tubes carefully. Supervision: Instructor guided.
intro_questions: What is the definition of atmospheric pressure?
State Bernoulli's theorem for incompressible flow.
What is the function of the pitot tube?

topics: Static, dynamic, and total pressure definitions
development.content:
Static, dynamic, and total pressure definitions
Pitot-static tube working principle
A.S.I calibration and indication

Indicated air speed (IAS) derivation
Rectified air speed (RAS) concept
Equivalent air speed (EAS) calculation

True air speed (TAS) determination
Position and instrument errors
Compressibility error effects

summary_questions: Differentiate between indicated air speed and true air speed.
Explain the cause of position error in A.S.I.
home_assignment_question: Calculate TAS from given IAS, altitude, and temperature data.

pft_rows.syllabus: Definition of streamline, stream tube, stream filament, ideal and real fluid, steady and turbulent flow, compressible and incompressible flow, viscous and in viscous flow, rotational and irrotational flow.
